summary.title: Platform Engineering: Build vs Buy
summary.one_liner: Learn a practical framework for deciding when a platform team should build an internal tool versus buy a vendor product, with cost, security, competitor, lock-in, and scale exceptions.
takeaways: Platform teams should favor building new services, niche problems without vendor ecosystems, and glue services, and buy commodities.
Build-cheaper claims need long-term maintenance costs, security patches, and engineering salary factored in; SaaS prices may rise about 10% per year.
Vendors can be worth avoiding for security reasons, competitor concerns, lock-in, or when they cannot scale to your needs.
A hub-and-spoke layer over vendors reduces lock-in, letting you swap vendors with less rework.
summary.summary: The author, a former Atlassian and Shopify security/platform engineer, shares a personal framework for the build-vs-buy question in platform engineering. The post explains that commodities should usually be bought, while teams should build innovative services, niche problems, and glue services. It then walks through exceptions: cheaper builds, vendor security concerns (with an Ngrok replacement example), competitor vendors, lock-in (with a Shopify device posture hub example), and scale limits (with a Confluence 10k-user example). It is an opinion essay with anecdotes rather than a step-by-step tutorial.
